summary: Joseph Haekel earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna (1931–1935). He spent his career there as an assistant to Koppers (1935), PD (1941), and succeeded Wilhelm Koppers as full professor and director in 1957.

Joseph Haroutunian was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied at AUB, Columbia (Ph.D. ~1928–1932), and Union Theological Seminary. He held posts at Wellesley (1932–1940), McCormick Theological Seminary (1940–1962), and the University of Chicago (1962–1968).

Joseph Light Wyatt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at St Augustine's College (~1864–1867) and Christ's College, Cambridge (M.A. ~1891–1893), later becoming a university teacher at the University of Cambridge in 1895.

Joseph Loizzo specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at Amherst, Harvard, and under Robert A. F. Thurman and Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche. He founded the Nalanda Institute and was a visiting scholar at Columbia University (attested 2007).

Joseph M. Kitagawa worked in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning his Ph.D. under Joachim Wach at the University of Chicago (~1947–1951). He spent his career at Chicago (~1951–1984), serving as professor, department head, and dean.

Joseph Mansion was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Ghent University (Ph.D. 1894–1899) and under Louis de La Vallée Poussin. He served as chargé de cours (1904) and extraordinary professor (1910) at the University of Liège.
Joseph Margolis was a philosopher who studied at Columbia University (~1947–1950, M.A.). He held the Laura H. Carnell Chair of Philosophy at Temple University (appointed 1991).

Joseph A. Marino specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ohio State and the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon and Collett Cox, later becoming an assistant professor at the University of Washington (2020, attested 2026).

Joseph Masson studied Indology and religious studies, earning a doctorate at KU Leuven (completed 1942). He taught at Institut Saint-Robert Bellarmin (~1944), the University of Namur, and was professor of Buddhism and mission theology at the Pontifical Gregorian University (1958).
Joseph Menrad was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich (~1884–1888, Ph.D.). He served as school director at Willibald-Gymnasium from 1921 to 1926.

Joseph Merkel worked in Indology. He taught at Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg (1810), served as a professor at Gymnasium Aschaffenburg (1818), and was court librarian at Hofbibliothek Aschaffenburg (1828).

Joseph Mullens was active in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Coward College, the University of London (B.A. ~1839–1841), the University of Edinburgh, and Williams College, later serving as foreign secretary of the London Missionary Society (1865).

Joseph Nadin Rawson worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at Jesus College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell and J. N. Farquhar, and served as professor at Serampore College (~1913–1937) and fellow at the University of Calcutta.

Joseph Needham studied at the University of Cambridge and Gonville and Caius College (~1918–1925). A scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, he was a fellow and master at Caius, reader at Cambridge (~1933–1966), and director of the Needham Research Institute (~1976–1990).
Joseph Peet was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Church Missionary Society College, Islington (1829). He served as principal of CMS College Kottayam (~1835–1837).

Joseph Prabhu is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied under Bernard Williams, Alasdair MacIntyre, and doctoral supervisor John N. Findlay, and held an associate professorship at California State University, Los Angeles (attested 1989, 2007).

Joseph Ratzinger studied religious studies at the University of Munich (~1947–1951) and Ducal Georgianum. He held academic posts at Munich (~1958–1959), Bonn (~1959–1963), Münster (~1963–1966), Tübingen (~1966–1969), and Regensburg (~1969–1977).

Joseph Rock worked in sinology and Tibetology. He held positions at the Mid-Pacific Institute (~1908), University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1908; 1911–1920), USDA (~1920–1922), Army Map Service (1944), Harvard-Yenching Institute (1946–1949), and Mills College.
Joseph Rupp was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich. He served as a gymnasium professor at Dom-Gymnasium Freising from 1850 to 1882.
Joseph S. Alter works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of California, Berkeley, and served as a professor at the University of Pittsburgh (attested 2008).
